newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada government still sees big 1997 job creation.
newsitem.headline: Canada government still sees big 1997 job creation.

text.p: The Canadian government still expects 300,000 to 350,000 new jobs this year despite disappointing job figures announced on Friday, a government official said on Friday.

Barry Campbell -- parliamentary secretary to Finance Minister Paul Martin, who was in New York on Friday -- told Parliament that analysts believe all the prospects for continued job growth were there.
He cited improved housing starts and housing resales and increased purchases and confidence.
"That will lead, as private sector forecasters continue to assert, to 300,000 to 350,000 new jobs in the coming year, when Canada will lead the industrialized countries in growth," Campbell said.
Member of Parliament John Williams of the opposition Reform Party shot back: "Great words...but no jobs."

The Bloc Quebecois's Francine Lalonde criticized the government for "a deteriorating situation for jobs in general and for women in particular." She said the women's employment situation "was going down the tubes."
Adult women lost 44,000 full-time jobs in February, Statistics Canada said. Including men, full-time employment fell by 38,000, and overall employment, including part-time jobs, fell by 18,700.
